title: The Carpenter Who Solved the Longitude Problem
subtitle: 解開經度難題的木匠：約翰．哈里森的航海鐘
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈John Harrison〉〈Longitude Act 1714〉〈Scilly naval disaster of 1707〉與 Royal Museums Greenwich 核對，2026-10-22

sources.title: Royal Museums Greenwich: Longitude found — the story of Harrison's timekeepers

beginner.title: A Clock That Saved Ships
paras: On 22 October 1707, four British warships hit rocks near the Isles of Scilly, off the coast of England. Between 1,400 and 2,000 sailors died. One reason was simple: the sailors did not know exactly where they were.
1707 年 10 月 22 日，四艘英國戰艦在英格蘭外海的錫利群島附近觸礁，造成 1,400 到 2,000 名水手死亡。原因之一很簡單：水手們不知道自己確切的位置。

At sea, finding latitude (how far north or south you are) was quite easy. But finding longitude (how far east or west you are) was very hard. In 1714, the British government offered a huge prize — up to £20,000 — to anyone who could solve this problem.
在海上，要找出緯度（你在多北或多南）相當容易，但要找出經度（你在多東或多西）卻非常困難。1714 年，英國政府提供一筆巨額獎金——最高兩萬英鎊——給任何能解決這個問題的人。

Why was time the key? The Earth turns 15 degrees every hour. If sailors knew the exact time at home and the time where their ship was, they could work out their longitude. But no clock could keep good time on a moving, wet ship.
為什麼時間是關鍵？地球每小時轉 15 度。如果水手知道家鄉的準確時間，也知道船所在地的時間，就能算出經度。但當時沒有任何時鐘能在搖晃又潮濕的船上準確計時。

John Harrison was a carpenter from a small village in England. He built clocks in his free time and taught himself. Over many years, he made four special clocks. The fourth one, called H4, looked like a large pocket watch. There is a story that when he was six and sick in bed, someone gave him a watch, and he spent hours listening to it and studying how it worked.
約翰．哈里森是英格蘭一個小村莊的木匠。他利用空閒時間做時鐘，靠自學起家。許多年來，他做了四座特別的時鐘。第四座叫 H4，看起來像一隻大型懷錶。有個傳說是這樣的：他六歲生病躺在床上時，有人給了他一隻錶，他花了好幾個小時聽它的聲音，研究它怎麼運作。

In 1761, H4 went on a ship to Jamaica. After 81 days, it was only 5 seconds slow. But the officials did not give Harrison the full prize. Finally, in 1773, when he was 80 years old, Parliament gave him £8,750. His idea changed the way ships found their way across the oceans.
1761 年，H4 搭船前往牙買加。81 天後，它只慢了 5 秒。但官員們並沒有把全額獎金頒給哈里森。最後在 1773 年，他 80 歲時，國會頒給他 8,750 英鎊。他的發明改變了船隻橫渡大洋時找路的方式。

intermediate.title: The Carpenter Who Solved the Longitude Problem
paras: On the night of 22 October 1707, a British fleet returning from the Mediterranean struck rocks off the Isles of Scilly. Four warships were lost, and between 1,400 and 2,000 sailors died — one of the worst disasters in British naval history. Among the causes was a problem that had troubled sailors for centuries: they could not accurately calculate their position.
1707 年 10 月 22 日夜裡，一支從地中海返航的英國艦隊在錫利群島外海觸礁。四艘戰艦沉沒，1,400 到 2,000 名水手喪生——這是英國海軍史上最慘重的災難之一。原因之一，是困擾水手好幾個世紀的問題：他們無法準確算出自己的位置。

Latitude could be found from the height of the sun or the stars, but longitude was another matter. In principle, the solution was clear. Because the Earth turns 15 degrees every hour, the difference between local time and the time at a home port reveals how far east or west a ship has travelled. In practice, no clock could stay accurate at sea, where ships rolled, temperatures changed and the air was wet and salty.
緯度可以從太陽或星星的高度求得，經度卻是另一回事。原則上，解法很清楚：因為地球每小時轉 15 度，當地時間和母港時間的差距，就能顯示船往東或往西走了多遠。但實際上，沒有任何時鐘能在海上保持準確——船身搖晃、溫度變化，空氣又潮又鹹。

In 1714 Parliament passed the Longitude Act, which created the Board of Longitude and offered rewards for a practical method. The top prize, £20,000, would go to a method accurate to within half a degree. Many experts expected the answer to come from astronomy. Instead, a serious challenge came from John Harrison, a self-taught clockmaker who had trained in his father’s trade as a carpenter.
1714 年，國會通過《經度法》，成立經度委員會，並為實用的方法提供獎金。最高獎金兩萬英鎊，要頒給誤差在半度以內的方法。許多專家預期答案會來自天文學。結果，一個強力的挑戰者卻是約翰．哈里森——一位自學的鐘錶匠，原本跟著父親學木匠手藝。

Harrison spent decades building a series of sea clocks, known today as H1, H2 and H3. His breakthrough came with H4, a large watch that was far smaller than his earlier sea clocks. In November 1761 it was sent on a voyage from Portsmouth to Jamaica. After 81 days at sea, it was just 5 seconds slow, an error in longitude of only about one nautical mile. Harrison, by then 68 years old, did not travel himself; the watch went in the care of his son, William.
哈里森花了幾十年打造一系列航海鐘，今天稱為 H1、H2 和 H3。他的突破是 H4——一隻比他先前的航海鐘小得多的大型懷錶。1761 年 11 月，它被送上一艘從樸茨茅斯開往牙買加的船。在海上 81 天後，它只慢了 5 秒，換算成經度誤差只有大約一海里。當時已經 68 歲的哈里森沒有親自上船；這隻錶交由他的兒子威廉照看。

Yet the Board was not satisfied. Its members suggested the result might be luck and demanded more trials. Harrison, deeply frustrated, eventually asked King George III for help. In 1773, at the age of 80, he received £8,750 from Parliament, though never the official prize. His story shows that a brilliant solution does not always win immediate recognition — and that persistence can matter as much as genius.
然而委員會並不滿意。委員們認為結果可能只是運氣，要求進行更多試驗。深感挫折的哈里森，最後向英王喬治三世求助。1773 年，80 歲的他從國會獲得 8,750 英鎊，卻始終沒有拿到正式的獎項。他的故事顯示：一個傑出的解答，不一定能立刻獲得認可——而堅持，可能和天才一樣重要。

advanced.title: Time, Distance and the Board of Longitude
paras: On 22 October 1707, four warships of a Royal Navy fleet struck rocks off the Isles of Scilly, near the British mainland. Between 1,400 and 2,000 sailors were lost, making it one of the worst maritime disasters in British naval history. Historians attribute the tragedy to several factors, including errors in charts and inadequate compasses, but one stands out: the navigators’ inability to calculate their position accurately. The disaster made vivid a problem that had limited ocean travel for centuries.
1707 年 10 月 22 日，皇家海軍一支艦隊的四艘戰艦，在靠近英國本土的錫利群島外海觸礁。1,400 到 2,000 名水手罹難，使它成為英國海軍史上最慘重的海難之一。歷史學家把這場悲劇歸因於多項因素，包括海圖錯誤和羅盤不良，但其中一項格外突出：領航員無法準確計算自己的位置。這場災難把一個限制遠洋航行好幾個世紀的問題，鮮明地攤在眾人眼前。

Determining latitude was relatively straightforward, since it could be read from the angle of the sun or the stars. Longitude, by contrast, depends on time. The Earth rotates through 15 degrees every hour, so a navigator who knows both the local time and the time at a reference point can convert the difference into distance east or west. Without such knowledge, sailors relied on dead reckoning — estimating position from speed, heading and elapsed time — which became increasingly unreliable on long voyages out of sight of land.
決定緯度相對簡單，因為可以從太陽或星星的角度讀出來。相較之下，經度取決於時間。地球每小時自轉 15 度，所以一位同時知道當地時間和參考點時間的領航員，就能把時差換算成往東或往西的距離。少了這項資訊，水手只能依賴航位推算法——從速度、航向和經過的時間估計位置——而在看不見陸地的長途航行中，這種方法越來越不可靠。

Parliament responded with the Longitude Act of 1714, which established the Board of Longitude and offered a graduated series of rewards: £10,000 for a practical method accurate to one degree, rising to £20,000 for accuracy within half a degree. Many in the scientific establishment assumed the solution would be astronomical. John Harrison, a joiner and self-taught clockmaker who grew up in Lincolnshire, pursued a mechanical answer instead: a clock robust enough to keep accurate time at sea.
國會的回應是 1714 年的《經度法》，它成立了經度委員會，並提供分級獎金：準確度在一度以內的實用方法可得一萬英鎊，在半度以內則提高到兩萬英鎊。科學界許多人認為解答會來自天文學。在林肯郡長大的細木匠、自學成材的鐘錶匠約翰．哈里森，卻追求一個機械式的答案：一座堅固到能在海上準確計時的時鐘。

His progress was slow but remarkable. It took five years to build his first sea clock, H1, which earned the Board’s support for further development. Two more large clocks followed before Harrison concluded, after some thirty years of experimentation, that the solution lay in a smaller watch. The result, H4, was tested on a voyage from Portsmouth to Kingston, Jamaica, which set sail on 18 November 1761. After 81 days and 5 hours, once its known daily rate had been allowed for, it was only 5 seconds slow — an error in longitude of about one nautical mile, far inside the Act’s requirement.
他的進展緩慢，卻非常驚人。他花了五年打造第一座航海鐘 H1，因此獲得委員會支持繼續研發。之後又做了兩座大型時鐘，經過約三十年的實驗，哈里森才認定答案在於更小的懷錶。成果 H4 在一趟從樸茨茅斯開往牙買加金斯敦的航程中接受測試，船於 1761 年 11 月 18 日啟航。81 天又 5 小時後，扣除已知的每日誤差率，它只慢了 5 秒——換算成經度誤差約一海里，遠優於法案的要求。

Success did not bring immediate reward. The Board suggested the accuracy might have been luck, questioned whether a timekeeper that had taken six years to build was truly practical, and demanded further trials. Harrison complained that he had been “extremely ill used” and eventually sought the help of King George III, who tested a later watch himself. In 1773, aged 80, Harrison received £8,750 from Parliament, although the official prize was never awarded to anyone. The episode reveals a recurring tension in the history of science: institutions must guard against lucky results, yet the same caution can delay recognition of genuine breakthroughs, especially when they come from outsiders.

成功並沒有帶來立即的報酬。委員會認為準確度可能只是運氣，質疑一個花了六年才做好的計時器是否真的實用，並要求更多試驗。哈里森抱怨自己受到「極不公平的對待」，最後向英王喬治三世求助，國王還親自測試了他後來的一隻懷錶。1773 年，80 歲的哈里森從國會獲得 8,750 英鎊，不過正式獎項始終沒有頒給任何人。這段插曲揭示了科學史上反覆出現的張力：機構必須提防僥倖的結果，然而同樣的謹慎，也可能延誤對真正突破的認可——尤其當突破來自圈外人時。

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why sailors could not find latitude at sea.
How four British warships were built in 1707.
How a carpenter built clocks that helped ships find their position.
How to make a pocket watch at home.
beginner.evidence: His idea changed the way ships found their way across the oceans.
beginner.why: 全文：木匠 Harrison 造鐘解決經度問題。
traps: 正反顛倒：找緯度很容易，難的是經度。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：1707 年是戰艦觸礁，不是建造。
捏造：文中沒有教人做錶。

beginner.q: What does “this problem” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: Finding longitude at sea.
Finding latitude at sea.
Building a huge prize.
Hitting rocks near England.
beginner.evidence: But finding longitude (how far east or west you are) was very hard.
beginner.why: 前一句說找經度非常難。
traps: 正反顛倒：找緯度很容易。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：獎金是解決問題的方法。
因果混淆：觸礁是這個問題造成的結果。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Harrison was a famous scientist from a big city.
Harrison made only one special clock.
The British government offered £8,750 as the prize in 1714.
After 81 days, H4 was only 5 seconds slow.
beginner.evidence: After 81 days, it was only 5 seconds slow.
traps: 正反顛倒：他是小村莊的木匠，自學造鐘。
數字錯位：他做了四座。
數字錯位：獎金最高兩萬英鎊，8,750 是 1773 年給他的。

beginner.q: Why was time the key to finding longitude?
options: Clocks on ships could stop the ship from rolling.
The time difference shows how far east or west a ship is.
Sailors could see the stars only at night to find longitude.
The Earth turns 15 degrees every minute of the day.
beginner.evidence: If sailors knew the exact time at home and the time where their ship was, they could work out their longitude.
traps: 捏造：文中說的是鐘在搖晃的船上無法準時，不是鐘能穩住船。
張冠李戴：看星星找的是緯度。
數字錯位：地球每小時轉 15 度。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Harrison’s son William invented the H4 watch.
Astronomers solved the longitude problem in 1714.
The Isles of Scilly disaster was caused only by bad weather.
Harrison solved the longitude problem but waited years for recognition.
intermediate.evidence: His story shows that a brilliant solution does not always win immediate recognition
traps: 張冠李戴：William 只是帶錶出海。
正反顛倒：解決問題的是鐘錶匠，不是天文學家。
捏造：原因是算不出位置。

intermediate.q: What does “In practice” in the second paragraph suggest?
options: Sailors practised using clocks every day.
The idea was simple, but carrying it out was difficult.
The solution worked well on every ship.
Ships rarely sailed far from home ports.
intermediate.evidence: In practice, no clock could stay accurate at sea
intermediate.why: 和前一句 In principle 對照：理論上簡單，實際上做不到。
traps: 字面誤讀：practice 在這裡不是練習。
正反顛倒：沒有鐘能在海上保持準確。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：母港只是用來對時的參考點。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The top prize went to a method accurate to one degree.
Harrison sailed to Jamaica with H4 himself.
Harrison was 68 when H4 was sent to Jamaica.
H4 was larger than the earlier sea clocks.
intermediate.evidence: Harrison, by then 68 years old, did not travel himself
traps: 數字錯位：最高獎金是半度以內。
正反顛倒：他沒有親自去，是兒子帶錶出海。
正反顛倒：H4 比之前的鐘小得多。

intermediate.q: Why did the Board refuse to give Harrison the prize at first?
options: They suspected the result might have been luck.
They thought the watch was too small to be practical.
They had already given the prize to an astronomer.
They believed latitude was more important than longitude.
intermediate.evidence: Its members suggested the result might be luck and demanded more trials.
traps: 捏造：文中只說委員會懷疑是運氣，沒說嫌錶太小。
正反顛倒：正式獎金從未頒給任何人。
捏造：文中沒比較經緯度的重要性。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To tell how Harrison solved longitude and why recognition came slowly.
To explain why compasses were inadequate in 1707.
To argue that astronomy is more reliable than clocks.
To describe King George III’s interest in science.
advanced.evidence: institutions must guard against lucky results, yet the same caution can delay recognition of genuine breakthroughs
advanced.why: 全文：哈里森的成就與遲來的肯定。
traps: 以偏概全：羅盤只是海難原因之一。

advanced.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “dead reckoning” in the second paragraph?
options: Reading the angle of the stars.
Counting the sailors lost at sea.
Estimating position from speed, direction and time.
Checking the time at a home port.
advanced.evidence: dead reckoning — estimating position from speed, heading and elapsed time
traps: 張冠李戴：看星星角度是找緯度的方法。
字面誤讀：dead 不是死亡。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：知道母港時間正是推算定位缺少的資訊。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Harrison’s first sea clock, H1, took six years to build.
The Act offered £10,000 for a method accurate to one degree.
King George III himself awarded Harrison the official prize.
Harrison was trained as an astronomer in the city of London.
advanced.evidence: £10,000 for a practical method accurate to one degree
traps: 數字錯位：H1 花五年，花六年的是 H4。
正反顛倒：正式獎金從未頒給任何人。
正反顛倒：他是木匠，自學造鐘。

advanced.q: What can be inferred about the Board’s attitude toward Harrison?
options: It trusted his results from the very start.
It wanted Harrison to give up clockmaking.
It doubted that longitude mattered at sea.
Its caution about luck delayed recognition of his real breakthrough.
advanced.evidence: the same caution can delay recognition of genuine breakthroughs, especially when they come from outsiders
traps: 正反顛倒：委員會懷疑是運氣。
過度推論：委員會一開始還支持他的研發。
正反顛倒：法案本身就是為了解決經度問題。

reflections: Harrison was an outsider — a carpenter, not a famous scientist. Why might experts sometimes doubt good ideas from outsiders?
Was the Board of Longitude right to demand more trials? Argue for one side.

Many in the scientific establishment assumed the answer would come from astronomy. It was not an astronomer but an outsider who offered the most serious challenge: John Harrison, a carpenter and self-taught clockmaker who grew up in Lincolnshire. Harrison set out to build a clock robust enough to keep accurate time on a rolling ship.
問題嚴重到國會在 1714 年通過《經度法》，為誤差在半度以內的實用方法提供最高 2 萬英鎊獎金。科學界許多人認定答案會來自天文學。然而提出最有力挑戰的不是天文學家，而是圈外人：在林肯郡長大、木匠出身、自學成才的鐘錶匠約翰・哈里森。他決心造出一座夠堅固、能在搖晃的船上保持準時的鐘。

His first sea clock, H1, took five years to build, and two more large clocks followed. Only after some thirty years of experimentation did Harrison conclude that the answer lay in a much smaller watch. The result, H4, was tested on a voyage from Portsmouth to Jamaica that set sail on 18 November 1761. After 81 days at sea, it was only 5 seconds slow—an error in longitude of about one nautical mile, far inside what the Act required.
他的第一座航海鐘 H1 花了五年才完成，之後又造了兩座大型的鐘。經過約三十年的試驗，哈里森才認定答案在一只小得多的錶上。成果 H4 在 1761 年 11 月 18 日從樸茨茅斯啟航前往牙買加接受測試。在海上 81 天後，它只慢了 5 秒——經度誤差約一海里，遠在法案要求的範圍之內。

Success, however, did not bring immediate reward. The Board of Longitude suggested the result might have been luck, questioned whether a timekeeper that had taken six years to build was truly practical, and demanded further trials. Complaining that he had been “extremely ill used,” Harrison eventually sought help from King George III, who tested a later watch himself. In 1773, at the age of 80, Harrison received £8,750 from Parliament, though the official prize was never awarded to anyone. His story reveals a lasting tension in science: caution protects us from lucky results, yet it can also delay the recognition of genuine breakthroughs, especially those made by outsiders.

然而成功並沒有立刻帶來獎賞。經度委員會認為結果可能只是運氣，質疑一個花了六年才造好的計時器是否真的實用，並要求更多測試。哈里森抱怨自己「受到極不公平的對待」，最後求助國王喬治三世，國王還親自測試了他後來的一只錶。1773 年，80 歲的哈里森從國會獲得 8,750 英鎊，但正式獎金從未頒給任何人。他的故事揭示科學裡長久的張力：謹慎能防止僥倖的結果，卻也可能延遲對真正突破的肯定——尤其當突破來自圈外人。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How the 1707 disaster led to the use of more accurate charts.
How a self-taught clockmaker tackled a problem that had long troubled sailors.
Why astronomers failed to win the prize offered by the Longitude Act.
How Parliament rewarded Harrison for building his early sea clocks.
questions.evidence: Harrison set out to build a clock robust enough to keep accurate time on a rolling ship
questions.why: 第一、二段鋪陳經度難題，第三到五段都在講哈里森如何解決，以及他遲來的肯定。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：海圖只是 1707 年海難的原因之一，文中沒說後來改用更準的海圖。
過度推論：文中只說「正式獎金從未頒給任何人」，沒說天文學家失敗。
張冠李戴：8,750 英鎊是 1773 年給的，不是因為早期的航海鐘；而且這只是第五段的細節。

questions.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “robust” in the third paragraph?
options: Strong and durable.
Small and portable.
Precise and accurate.
Cheap and practical.
questions.evidence: a clock robust enough to keep accurate time on a rolling ship
questions.why: 要在搖晃（rolling）的船上照常運作，鐘必須「堅固耐用」。注意 robust enough to keep accurate time：準確是結果，robust 是讓它能準確的條件。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：「小」是 H4 的特徵（a much smaller watch），不是 robust 的意思。
因果混淆：accurate 就寫在後面，但它是 robust 帶來的結果，不是 robust 本身的意思。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：practical 出現在第五段，是委員會的質疑。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The 1707 disaster was caused only by the navigators’ failure to find their position.
Sailors could find longitude easily by reading the angle of the sun.
After 81 days at sea, H4 was slower than the Act allowed.
Dead reckoning became less reliable the longer a ship sailed out of sight of land.
questions.evidence: a method that grew less and less reliable on long voyages out of sight of land
questions.why: 正解改寫自第二段 grew less and less reliable on long voyages out of sight of land。
traps: 以偏概全：原文說 several factors，only 錯。
張冠李戴：看太陽角度找的是 latitude，不是 longitude。
正反顛倒：只慢 5 秒，far inside what the Act required。

questions.q: Which of the following shows the correct order of events? a. Harrison concludes that a smaller watch is needed. b. The Longitude Act is passed. c. H4 is tested on a voyage to Jamaica. d. King George III tests one of Harrison’s watches.
options: a → b → c → d
b → c → a → d
b → a → c → d
b → a → d → c
questions.evidence: Only after some thirty years of experimentation did Harrison conclude
questions.why: 1714 法案 → 約三十年試驗後改做小錶 → 1761 年 H4 出海測試 → 委員會刁難後求助國王，國王測試的是 a later watch。
traps: 時序顛倒：法案是一切的起點。
時序顛倒：先決定做小錶，才有 H4 出海。
關鍵字陷阱：國王測的是 a later watch（H4 之後），所以 d 在 c 之後。

mixed.prompt: Many experts assumed the solution would be [47], but Harrison’s answer was mechanical. Even so, the Board of Longitude was slow to [48] his achievement.
mixed.why: 第一格：第三段 astronomy 是名詞，be 動詞後面要用形容詞 astronomical，和 mechanical 對照。第二格：第五段名詞 recognition 改成動詞 recognize（to 後接原形）。

mixed.q: Which of the following are true about John Harrison? Choose ALL that apply.
options: He was a carpenter who taught himself to make clocks.
He finished H4 within five years.
He experimented for about thirty years before turning to a smaller watch.
He received the official £20,000 prize.
He sought help from the king.
He received £8,750 from the Board of Longitude.
mixed.why: A、C、E 見第三到五段。B 張冠李戴（五年的是 H1）；D 與原文相反（正式獎金從未頒出）；F 張冠李戴（錢是國會給的，不是委員會）。

mixed.q: What method did sailors rely on when they did not know the local time and the time at a home port?
mixed.why: 第二段 Without such knowledge, sailors relied on “dead reckoning”。
